interest: This docket sheet provides valuable insight into Allied surveillance of Axis intelligence networks operating in neutral Francoist Spain during World War II. It illustrates how Japanese representatives sought to exploit Spanish infrastructure—such as secretly utilizing the Malaga Broadcasting Service for propaganda or communications—and gathered intelligence on American military affairs through contacts in Madrid like Matsuo. Furthermore, the document highlights the inter-agency flow of intelligence between J. Edgar Hoover's FBI and the State Department, diplomatic sensitivity regarding U.S. press coverage that provoked protests from the Spanish Ambassador, and State Department registry practices for non-jacketed intelligence files.
overview: This file consists of a Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet for decimal file 894.20252, categorized as a non-jacket case under the subject 'Alleged subversive Japanese activities in Spain.' Covering communications from March 1942 through April 1944, the docket sheet indexes three separate documents concerning Japanese espionage, propaganda, and intelligence operations conducted in Spain during World War II. These include a March 23, 1942 notification from J. Edgar Hoover of the Department of Justice reporting Japanese arrangements to secretly use the Malaga Broadcasting Service; a March 11, 1942 transmittal by Fletcher Warren of the State Department enclosing New York Times and Washington Times-Herald clippings that prompted a protest from the Spanish Ambassador; and an April 19, 1944 telegram (#1356) from Ambassador Carlton J. H. Hayes in Spain containing a paraphrase of an instruction sent in plain Japanese to Matsuo in Madrid requesting intelligence on American military affairs, cross-referenced to file 862.20200/255.

subfiles.about: A Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet indexing three communications concerning alleged Japanese subversive and intelligence activities in Spain between 1942 and 1944.
subfiles.summary: This State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet summarizes three records filed under decimal classification 894.20252 regarding Japanese subversive and espionage activities in Spain from 1942 to 1944. Item 1 records a March 23, 1942 report from J. Edgar Hoover of the Justice Department regarding secret arrangements by the Japanese Foreign Council in Spain to utilize the Malaga Broadcasting Service. Item 2 notes a March 11, 1942 transmittal by Fletcher Warren of two press clippings from the New York Times and Washington Times-Herald that drew a formal protest from the Spanish Ambassador. Item 3 cites an April 19, 1944 telegram from Ambassador Carlton J. H. Hayes paraphrasing instructions in plain Japanese sent to Matsuo in Madrid soliciting U.S. military intelligence, with a cross-reference to file 862.20200/255.
